schema_notes: materials: the task files and folders given by the organisers (README.md, docs/, data/ ...). Never team output (.hackathon-kit/, run/, submission/). Every line in them with an outcome word (무효, 0점, 반려, 감점, 실격, 불합격, void, penalty ...) or a target word (포함률, 신뢰구간, coverage, calibration ...) must be named by a rule source ('file:line' exactly as the error shows it) or listed in not_rules [{at, why}]. Files the scan cannot read (PDF, legacy Office, broken archives) must be opened and noted in unscanned_reviewed [{file, note}].

Rules: consequence VOID, ZERO or REJECT (breach voids results, gives zero points or rejects), PENALTY (points or cost per unit beyond a limit), TARGET (points lost on either side of a target, such as interval coverage) or SOFT (decides no score or acceptance).

VOID/ZERO/REJECT: {id, rule (quote), source (file:line), consequence, term, candidates:[{meaning, source}], decision}. candidates: every reading of the term that some document, column, header or definition supports; run `hard_rules.py scan --root <task folder> --path <material> --term <word>`.

decision: ALL_MEANINGS; OFFICIAL_ANSWER {official_answer:{quote, source, meaning}} where source is one of answer_sources [{path, sha256}] (recorded replies of organisers, never team files) and the quote names the term; SINGLE_MEANING only with exactly one candidate and scan_hits equal to the scan count of the term; COST_EXCEPTION {exception:{meanings_kept, loss_all_meanings, loss_if_wrong, probability_wrong, basis}} only when loss_all_meanings > probability_wrong * loss_if_wrong. A document that says how a field is recorded, or which document takes precedence, does not decide what the rule refers to. 'Not in the documents' is not an official answer.

Numeric limit (CP1): limit, direction ('max' or 'min'), inclusive (true if a value equal to the limit is allowed), unit, statistic (what is compared: each lot, mean, maximum, 95th percentile, per week), stress_plan (at least two of demand_up, capacity_down, timing_shift, mix_shift, data_noise, other), uses_model (true/false), metric_source (evaluator, simulator, estimated; uses_model true means estimated), for estimated known_real_cases (at least 5) and explained_definition, and margin (> 0, in the unit of the limit; suggested 10% of the limit or at least 1 for a count) with margin_basis; the margin may not be lowered after CP1. A void rule without a numeric threshold gives no_numeric_limit_reason.

Final checks for VOID/ZERO/REJECT: checks:[{meaning, scenario, violations, evidence:{path, sha256}}] for every kept meaning; the evidence JSON must state the same violations (and value). Any violation of a kept meaning must be fixed before submission. Numeric limits add scenario_kind ('public' replay or 'stress' harsher than the given data), stress_type and stress_param for stress, and value inside the limit and inside the CP1 margin (at most limit - margin for max, at least limit + margin for min); every planned stress for every kept meaning; stress values may not be milder than the public replay. Estimated values add estimated:true, risk_bound (one-sided 95% bound on the side of the limit, strictly beyond the estimate) inside the limit and the margin, and estimator_validation {explained, total} with total >= known_real_cases and explained >= half of total.

PENALTY at final: tradeoff:{chosen, chosen_expected_loss, alternatives:[{label, expected_loss, at_limit?}] (at least two, one at_limit:true), evidence} whose evidence JSON states chosen_expected_loss and alternatives {label: expected_loss}. Choose the lowest expected loss (uncertainty included in the expected loss).

TARGET: {target, tolerance} (tolerance above 5% of the target needs tolerance_quote found in tolerance_source); at final observed:{value, evidence} within target +/- tolerance, evidence JSON stating value.

baseline_plan (CP1): [{output, metric, unit, better: 'lower'|'higher', metric_quote, metric_file (the task sentence defining the scored metric), baselines: [current|uniform|pooled|no_action|other, ...], per_group: true|false (pooled required when true), search_plan: [at least two methods], min_gain (> 0, metric units), holdout_kind: 'time' with tuning_until and evaluated_from as ISO dates (evaluation after the last tuning day) or 'group' with holdout_groups}]. Use no_baseline_reason only when nothing will be tuned. Never tune on the evaluation period.

baseline_guard (final): one entry per planned output (or dropped_reason in the plan): {output, submitted (evaluation-period value of the submitted output), baselines:[{label, kind, value, admissible?, violated_rule?, violation_evidence?}], same boundary as the plan, artifact:{path, sha256} of the submitted output, evidence (JSON with submitted and baselines {label: value}), optimization:{rounds:[{method, value (tuning-period score), candidate_sha256, admissible?}], chosen (index of the submitted round), evidence (JSON with rounds: [values]), bound?, bound_method?, bound_evidence? (JSON with bound), stop? {reason: 'deadline', round_minutes, remaining_minutes}}}. A baseline is set aside only with violated_rule (a rule id here) and violation_evidence stating violations >= 1. The submitted value must not be worse than any admissible baseline; the chosen round must be the best admissible round and its candidate the submitted artifact. Stop within 1% of a proven bound, on a plateau (last two rounds near the best, each gaining less than min_gain) or when less than one round of time is left.

Record it in V27_EVIDENCE as records.hard_rules {path, sha256}. When the CP1 review passes, copy it unchanged to .hackathon-kit/run/HARD_RULES_CP1.json and record records.hard_rules_cp1; final compares with that copy and allows only additions (rules, candidates, stress types, baselines, methods, known cases) and moves to ALL_MEANINGS or to a later official answer. CP1 and final review scopes must include the current SHA256.
